test.name: Routes a hint-review request to the search-hints agent
test.description: The user asks /research to check the FamilySearch hints on Patrick Flynn (LZNY-BRF). A hint review is an entry point, not a downstream destination (research/SKILL.md, "Hint review"): the router spawns @plugin:search-hints with personId and projectPath, and search-hints decides each hint and logs its decisions. search-hints is stubbed with a realistic review whose decisions are already logged, so the test also pins that the router relays it once and ends the turn, with no second spawn and no log write of its own (test_hint_review_runs_once). e2e can never reach this route (person_record_matches is in BLOCKED_TREE_TOOLS), so this test is its only check (issue #2029). The message enters /research ("keep researching … parentage") and asks for the hint check inside it; a bare "check the hints" is matched by search-hints' own description and never reaches the router.

input.user_message: /research Keep researching Patrick Flynn's parentage — and start by checking the FamilySearch hints on him (FamilySearch ID LZNY-BRF): are any of them valid?

stub_skills.response:
Hint ark:/61903/1:1:M70C: accept → log_006 — 1870 United States Federal Census, confidence 3; Patrick Flynn, 25, born Ireland, in Thomas Flynn's household, Schuylkill.
Hint ark:/61903/1:1:M80C: accept → log_007 — 1880 United States Federal Census, confidence 2; the index reads Glynn but the image reads Flynn, 35, coal miner, born Ireland.
Hint ark:/61903/1:1:MDEF: already linked by pe_005 — Pennsylvania Death Certificates, confidence 2; extracted as src_004, linked to I1 by pe_005.
Accepted for extraction: {ark:/61903/1:1:M70C, log_006}, {ark:/61903/1:1:M80C, log_007}

---

Three records FamilySearch suggests for Patrick were looked at. The 1870 census, which FamilySearch rates a moderate match, shows him at 25 in his father Thomas's household, and was accepted. The 1880 census, a weaker match on FamilySearch's scale, was indexed under the wrong surname, but the page itself reads Flynn and fits him, so it was accepted too. His 1908 death certificate is already part of this research.

Next, the details of the two accepted records are added to the project.

judge_context: This is a ROUTING test. The only assertion that matters is whether @plugin:search-hints is the first hand-off. A deterministic validator (test_routes_to_expected_skill) owns that check — do not grade the routing decision yourself.
The delegation should carry personId (LZNY-BRF) and projectPath, and no accept/reject verdicts — none was stated by the researcher.

search-hints is stubbed with a review whose decisions are already logged. The router should relay the researcher-facing part and end the turn, offering the next step. Spawning search-hints again, asking the researcher to decide the hints, or logging the hints itself is wrong — a deterministic validator checks the spawn count and that the router wrote no log entry.

ROUTING IS NOT YOURS TO GRADE. The hand-off is asserted deterministically by test_routes_to_expected_skill, which reads the PreToolUse hook records. Do NOT score Correctness or Completeness on whether the router reached the right callee.

The reply must carry the meaning of search-hints' summary: the 1870 census was accepted, the 1880 census was accepted though indexed under the wrong surname, and the 1908 death certificate is already part of the research. Rewording, reformatting and added text are acceptable (lead, 2026-11-03). A reply that drops one of these findings, states one differently, or asks the researcher to accept or reject the hints fails Correctness or Completeness.
